title: lsass.exe writing C:\Windows\debug\PASSWD.LOG on scranton
rationale: F65 documents a Sysmon file-create event showing lsass.exe (PID 748) creating C:\Windows\debug\PASSWD.LOG on scranton.dmevals.local, with a CreationUtcTime of 2020-03-12 suggesting a pre-existing file re-touched rather than a fresh dump — a credential-named artifact on the compromised host, best fitting OS Credential Dumping (T1003) at low confidence.

title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks by PowerShell on scranton and wsmprovhost on nashua
rationale: All five findings describe the same action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff/0x1FFFFF (PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) with an UNKNOWN-module CallTrace, corroborated by the 4663 object-access event on \Device\HarddiskVolume2\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, plus the same 0x1f3fff mask used by wsmprovhost.exe on nashua.dmevals.local. F05 and F39 explicitly note no separate LSA-secrets or auth-process modification artifact exists, so the best-fitting in-scope technique is LSASS memory dumping (T1003.001).

title: PowerShell screen-capture function (Invoke-ScreenCapture) run by pbeesly on scranton
rationale: F12 documents pbeesly defining and invoking Invoke-ScreenCapture on scranton.dmevals.local, a background job using System.Windows.Forms/System.Drawing CopyFromScreen to capture the screen — GUI input capture, matching T1056.002.

title: PowerShell script blocks are credential/file collection, not forced authentication
rationale: F27 documents that the 4104 script blocks on scranton.dmevals.local under pbeesly are recursive enumeration of credential-named user files compressed to $env:APPDATA\Draft.Zip and a System.Drawing bitmap steganography loader (monkey.png) — collection/credential-access behavior with no UNC/WebDAV coercion or outbound authentication trigger, so it is not T1187.

title: APT29-style PowerShell screen capture and exfil present but unrelated to cookie theft
rationale: F30 documents the same pbeesly PowerShell tooling on scranton.dmevals.local (Invoke-ScreenCapture, Invoke-Exfil with 7-Zip password 'lolol' and WebDAV copy to \\192.168.0.4\webdav) but explicitly notes it does not touch browser cookie stores, so it is not T1539 activity.

title: Post-exploitation PowerShell credential toolkit run by pbeesly on scranton
rationale: These findings all describe the same pbeesly PowerShell session on scranton.dmevals.local loading a multi-function toolkit from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite (psversion.ps1/readme.ps1): Invoke-Discovery, Invoke-Persistence, Get-PrivateKeys, Invoke-ScreenCapture, Get-Keystrokes, Get-Clipboard, credential-file harvesting, Invoke-Exfil and Invoke-BeachCleanup, plus hidden encoded PowerShell, a Javasoft registry Invoke-Expression one-liner, hostui.exe elevation and a monkey.png steganographic loader. The unifying action is harvesting unsecured credentials and credential-bearing files from the host, best fitting T1552.

title: Hardcoded credentials in attacker PowerShell tooling and explicit-credential logons to NASHUA
rationale: These findings all concern credentials found in files and attacker tooling: Invoke-Exfil embedding plaintext credentials ($UserName 'cozy', $Password 'MyCozyPassw0rd!') and mapping \\192.168.0.4\webdav, pbeesly's explicit-credential logons to NASHUA, the nashua PowerShell harvesting of *pass*/*login*/*admin*/*vpn* files into working.zip, the password-protected RAR archive (-hpfGzq5yKw) with sdelete wiping, and accesschk.exe writing passwordsDB on scranton. The unifying action is credentials in files, matching T1552.001.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exported machine certificate private keys to .pfx on scranton
rationale: F31 and F59 describe the same action: pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local running Get-PrivateKeys (from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1), which enumerates cert:\LocalMachine and calls Export-PfxCertificate for every certificate with a Thumbprint, writing private keys to $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<random>.pfx protected by hardcoded password 'saribas', with the .pfx file creation and certificate registry blob events corroborating it. This is private-key theft, matching T1552.004.

title: No DHCP spoofing; NDIS Capture service toggle is a brief reverted change
rationale: F49 documents that no DHCP traffic (UDP 67/68) exists in any dataset; the only anomaly is a 4-second toggle of the Microsoft NDIS Capture service start type on scranton.dmevals.local, consistent with a packet-capture driver being briefly enabled rather than a rogue DHCP server, and the xDNSServerAddress script blocks on newyork are legitimate DSC. Not T1557.003.

title: PsExec lateral movement with plaintext credentials and python.exe payload on nashua
rationale: These findings describe the same activity: pbeesly using PsExec64.exe with plaintext credentials (-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by) to install PSEXESVC and launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on \\NASHUA, the 4648 explicit-credential logons being PsExec-driven reuse of one account (not spraying, not MFA interception), and the PyInstaller python.exe executing as a child of PSEXESVC.exe. This is remote service execution/lateral movement, not credential access, so it is out-of-scope (T1021).
